paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Israel is about to win, and Moses wants them ready for that moment. He says it three ways. It is not because of their righteousness, not because of their uprightness of heart, and not because of anything in them. The LORD goes across ahead of them "as a consuming fire," and He keeps "the promise He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob" (Deuteronomy 9:3, 5).

So why does Moses dig up the golden calf right before the victory? Because a people who forget where the win came from start to think they earned it. He tells them, "Remember this, and never forget how you provoked the LORD your God in the wilderness" (Deuteronomy 9:7). Then the shattered tablets, the dust in the stream and Moses face down for forty days all say the same thing: Israel was held up by a God who listens, and Moses prays "But they are Your people, Your inheritance" (Deuteronomy 9:29).

And that's good news for you and me, baker. You don't have to pretend your edges are sharp, because mine were BLURRY and I got called out of that junk drawer anyway. God gave a second set of tablets, kept His promise, and told Moses, "Get up. Continue your journey ahead of the people" (Deuteronomy 10:11). So when a win comes, don't take the credit. Say thank You to the One who went ahead of you, and keep walking. The story isn't over, friend, because Moses still has more to say.
